title: The 5R Permissions: Five Things You May Do

zones.label: Retain
zones.summary: Make, own, and control copies of the resource.
facts: Download it, duplicate it, store it, and manage your own copy.
Keep the file, not just a link. A bookmark is not a copy.
Retain matters because websites change and disappear.

zones.label: Reuse
zones.summary: Use the resource in its original, unaltered form.
facts: In a class, a study group, a workshop, a website, or a video.
The moment you alter it, even to fix a typo, you have moved to revise.

zones.label: Revise
zones.summary: Adapt, adjust, modify, or alter the resource itself.
facts: Fix an error, update a statistic, translate, lower the reading level, or add local examples.
Adding captions or alt text is also a revision.
Revise is the permission that separates an open resource from a merely free one.

zones.label: Remix
zones.summary: Combine the work with other open material to create something new.
facts: Revise changes one work; remix joins two or more.
Remixing requires that the licenses of the parts are compatible. Chapter 2 explains how.

zones.label: Redistribute
zones.summary: Share copies of the original, revised, or remixed work with others.
facts: Post it on a website, email it to colleagues, or upload it to a repository.
Redistribution is what lets one teacher's improvement reach every other teacher.
Keep a credit note and the license notice with the file when you pass it on.

quiz.question: You add alt text to every image in an openly licensed chapter. Which permission is that?
quiz.explanation: Adding alt text changes the work, and changing a work is revising it.

quiz.question: You show an openly licensed diagram, unchanged, on the projector. Which permission is that?
quiz.explanation: Using a work as it is, in your class, is reuse.

quiz.question: You copy the full set of source files of an open lab manual to an external drive. Which permission is that?
quiz.explanation: Keeping your own copy for safekeeping is retaining.

quiz.question: You combine two chapters from different open textbooks and a public-domain map into one unit packet. Which permission is that?
quiz.explanation: Combining two or more works into something new is remixing.

quiz.question: A colleague asks for the open worksheet you use, and you email them an unchanged copy. Which permission is that?
quiz.explanation: Sharing copies with others is redistributing.
